title: Your first choice in Gemini
summary: Use the same tiny puzzle to see when extra thinking helps.

intro.what: Gemini is an app you can talk or type to. A model is the part that makes the answer. Think of the app as a radio and the model as the station you choose.
intro.features: Chat answers a message. Tasks can work on a longer job. Deep Research can look for sources and build a report.
intro.exchange: Ask it to sort two pretend messages into “delivery problem” and “password question.” Check each label.
intro.m365: Turn a four-line meeting note into a checklist. Make sure the time stays the same.
intro.developer: Ask it to write the rules for a guessing game. Try a winning guess and a losing guess.
sources: Google · the Gemini app and feature directory
Google · AI Studio Playground and Run settings

sections.title: Find the model menu
paragraphs: Open Gemini on your iPad. Tap the model name near the message box. Auto lets the app choose. What you see depends on your account and its limits. These are the choices Google lists for personal accounts.
sources: Google Help · model choices on iPad

sections.title: Try two thinking levels
paragraphs: Type “The bus leaves at 9. The walk takes 10 minutes. What is the latest time I can start walking?” You can check the answer on a clock. Now add “I want to arrive five minutes early.” Check both answers. Try a higher thinking level if your first answer misses a rule. More thinking can use more of your account allowance.
sources: Google Help · model choices on iPad
Google AI Studio · choosing a model

exercise.prompt: What answers should the two versions give?
answer: 8:50 for the first walk. Leave at 8:45 to arrive five minutes early.

sections.title: Pick chat, Tasks or Deep Research
paragraphs: Use chat to fix a sentence. Use Tasks for a job you want to check on later. Try Deep Research when you need several sources. Example: “Find two public guides to growing beans indoors. Show where each says how much light beans need.” Read the plan first. Open both guides before you share the result.
sources: Google · how Deep Research plans and reports

title: Choose a model for your own app
summary: Find the exact model name an app must send, then test it on a case you can solve.

intro.what: An API lets one app ask another app for help. Your program sends a request with a model ID. An ID is the exact label the service expects.
intro.features: Google lists models for reading, writing, pictures and more. Each listing tells you what goes in, what comes out and how much fits.
intro.exchange: Give a model a made-up mail warning. Check whether it keeps the error number.
intro.m365: Ask for the date on a sample meeting flyer. Leave the date blank on one test.
intro.developer: Build a screen that reads a flyer and lets you fix any wrong fields.
sources: Google AI Studio · choosing a model
Google AI Studio · full model directory

sections.title: Read the ID and pick a first test
paragraphs: Use the exact ID from the second column when your program calls Google. Use these jobs to try the choices. Compare the results with answers you know.
sources: Google AI Studio · choosing a model
Google · model release and retirement dates

rows: Sort a pile of short notes by topic.
Read the time from a flyer and answer a second question.
Follow a rule with several exceptions.
Find which step made a score change twice.
Try a hard math or code problem on an older app.

sections.title: Leave space for the answer
paragraphs: A token is a small piece of text. The context window is like one desk with room for the question, your files and the reply. For {{model.google.carbon.name}}, that shared space fits {{model.google.context}}. The usual reply limit is {{model.google.max-out}}. Very long replies use a special setting. A whole video can go in and a written list of scenes can come out. Use a video maker when you need a new movie.
sources: Google AI Studio · full model directory

sections.title: Watch for a model change
paragraphs: Some older choices include {{model.google.older-flash.name}} and {{model.google.pro-preview.name}}. A preview can change. Save a few sample questions with correct answers. Run them before and after a switch.

Google scheduled two changes for {{model.google.redirect-date}}. Requests to {{model.google.old-pro.id}} will go to {{model.google.new-flash.id}}. Requests to {{model.google.old-flash.id}} will go to {{model.google.lite.id}}. Check the new price and compare the answers before you let your app use the change.
sources: Google AI Studio · full model directory

title: Give Gemini the right page or file
summary: Give Gemini a tab, a file or a set of notes. Find the line behind an answer, then turn the notes into something you can study.

intro.what: Gemini can read a shared browser page, work with a linked app or answer from files you select in Gemini Notebook.
intro.features: Chrome can share a tab. Connected Apps can read files you allow. Gemini Notebook puts sources, chat and Studio side by side. Studio turns the same pages into maps, audio or study cards.
intro.exchange: Put two sample mail rules in a notebook. Ask which one catches a blank subject.
intro.m365: Find which of two meeting notes gives the updated time. Check its date.
intro.developer: Put the rules and help page for a game in one notebook. Find a rule the help page forgot.
sources: Google · Gemini in Chrome and device availability
Google Help · source selection and citations in Gemini Notebook
Google Help · the notebook and its Studio tools

sections.title: Read two tabs in Chrome
paragraphs: On a supported computer, open two public product pages. Open Gemini in Chrome and share those tabs. Ask “How thick a sheet can each cutter cut? Give the unit and the line where you found it.” Read those lines yourself. A machine might hold a board that is thicker than it can cut. On iPad, use the mobile help for the controls you see.
sources: Google · Gemini in Chrome and device availability

sections.title: Look in a linked app
paragraphs: A linked app gives Gemini a way to look things up with your permission. Try this with sample mail in an account you can use. Ask it to find the newest practice meeting note and show its time. Open the message. Check whether a later note moved the meeting. You can turn off a connection in the account settings.

sections.title: Study a small set of sources
paragraphs: Add two notes to Gemini Notebook. In the first write “Bring a hat.” In the second write “Meet at 9.” Select only the first note. Ask when to meet. The selected note gives no time. Now select both. Ask again. Follow the answer’s source link to “Meet at 9.” Check what happens when you take that note away.
sources: Google Help · check an answer against its sources

sections.title: Find new sources inside the notebook
paragraphs: Open your notebook on a computer. Look for Sources on the left. Enter a question there and choose Web. Fast Research brings back a short list you can open. Deep Research takes longer and brings back a report plus links. Google limits Deep Research to adult accounts.

Choose View. Open a result and find the line that answers your question. Import the pages you want. In Sources, clear the check beside any page you cannot verify. With only your checked pages selected, ask the question in Chat. Follow its citation, the little link back to the source.
sources: Google Help · find and import sources with Fast or Deep Research
Google Help · check an answer against its sources

sections.title: Pick a Studio output for the job
paragraphs: Suppose you have two rule sheets for a game. A friend wants to hear the rules. A player wants to see what changed. Open Studio in the notebook and pick a format for each person. Use the same two sheets for both.
Slide Decks and Infographics need an eligible adult account. If a tool is missing on your tablet, open the book beside a computer browser for that activity.

rows: Hear two hosts discuss the rules. In a new English recording, turn on Interactive Mode and choose Join to ask them a question.
Watch a narrated tour of the rules. Pause on one picture and check its label against the rule sheet.
Open the map in Studio and expand a branch. Select a point to ask about that part of the game in Chat.
Show one rule per slide. Check the winning score on the slide before you teach it.
Make a single picture to hang by the game. Check that its labels match the rules.
Put dates in one column and winning scores in another. Read across each row to catch a swapped score.
Set the difficulty. Mark cards you missed and practice those again. In a quiz, try Hint or Explain, then retake it. This adapts your practice to what you need.

sections.title: Check the version your friends will see
paragraphs: Open a finished map, table or slide beside the original rule sheets. Find a claim you can check, such as “The winning score is 12.” Look for both the score and the date on the sheet. If the source later changes, make a fresh Studio output and check it again. Older outputs can keep the old rule.
sources: Google Help · find and import sources with Fast or Deep Research

title: Build a first app with Google’s tools
summary: Try a rule in AI Studio. Then make a small app and test it as a player.

intro.what: AI Studio is a place to try ideas with Google models. Antigravity is a coding tool that can open a project folder and work on its files.
intro.features: Playground lets you test a prompt. Build can make a working preview. Antigravity lets you read the plan, try the app and inspect the edits.
intro.exchange: Test whether a mail helper shows a blank date when a message gives no date.
intro.m365: Build a small meeting list that keeps two times if a flyer lists two sessions.
intro.developer: Build a word game with a Guess button. Check a win, a miss and a blank guess.
sources: Google · AI Studio Playground and Run settings
Google · Build mode, sharing and API keys
Google Antigravity · app and change review

sections.title: Test one rule first
paragraphs: Open Playground in AI Studio. Type “Read this flyer. Give the title, date and every showtime. Use null when there is no date.” Try “Puppet show. Times 2 and 4.” You should get both times and a missing date. Compare {{model.google.lite.name}} and {{model.google.hydrogen.name}} on the same flyer. Structured output can put each piece in a named box that your app can read. Still check what each box holds.
sources: Google · AI Studio Playground and Run settings

sections.title: Make the first screen
paragraphs: Open Build in AI Studio. Ask for a flyer checker with two panels. The left side should keep the original flyer. The right side should show the date and times, with a way to fix them. Paste the same flyer and try a correction. If your app uses a paid API key, keep that secret on its server. A browser sends its own files to anyone who opens the page.
sources: Google · Build mode, sharing and API keys

sections.title: Check a real project
paragraphs: Open a practice folder in Antigravity. Ask for a search box for book titles. Ask to see a plan first. Try one title that exists and one that does not. Clear the box. The full shelf should return. Open the list of changed files and check each one before you save the change to the shared project.
sources: Google Antigravity · app and change review
Google Antigravity · browser tools and availability

title: Make a picture, a clip or a sound
summary: Start by naming the file you want to have at the end.

intro.what: Google offers different tools for different kinds of media. One can draw a picture. Another can listen to speech and write down the words.
intro.features: You can edit a still picture, make a short clip, create music or read a script aloud. The app and the API may offer different choices.
intro.exchange: Read a picture of a made-up error box. Check that its last digit was copied correctly.
intro.m365: Make a short spoken version of a sample meeting note. Listen for the time and date.
intro.developer: Draw a game icon. Shrink it to button size and see if you can still tell what it is.
sources: Google · image creation in the Gemini app

sections.title: Draw a cover and change one detail
paragraphs: Ask for a gold key on dark blue cloth. Leave space at the top for a title. Next ask for a darker cloth. Check that the key still has the same shape. Add your final title in a text editor so you can fix the spelling.

Image choices include {{model.google.banana.name}} for edits, {{model.google.banana-lite.name}} for quick tries and {{model.google.banana-pro.name}} for hard layouts. Google also lists {{model.google.banana-older.name}}. Look for the choices your account offers.
sources: Google · image creation in the Gemini app

sections.title: Turn the cover into a moving shot
paragraphs: Use the book cover as the first picture. Ask for a still book while the camera moves slowly closer. Google’s app moved from {{model.google.veo.name}} to its newer video tool. The API offers {{model.google.video.name}} for short clips. Play the full clip. Does the title stay the same? Does the book keep all four corners? For a world the viewer can steer, Google also offers {{model.google.genie.name}}.

sections.title: Choose the right kind of sound
paragraphs: Listen for the one detail that matters. If the script says “gate fifteen,” play the sound back and check that it does not say “gate fifty.”

rows: {{model.google.lyria.name}}. Ask for four calm bars with a clear ending.
{{model.google.transcribe.name}}. Check the numbers against the sound.
Gemini Live in the app or the Live API in your own app.
